approve_payslip.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:payrolls.write`

Approves a draft payslip: it stops being a draft and is posted to the ledger.

Payroll is what the Human Resources gem sells, so this endpoint requires it to be active on the account and answers 402 when it is not.

The operation is not idempotent: approving a payslip that is already approved answers 409 rather than reporting a success that did not happen. It also answers 409 when the accounting period of the payslip date is closed, or when the payslip is a retroactive receipt (`gratificacion_no_cuantificable` or `atrasos`) whose accumulated contribution bases have changed since it was calculated — that one has to be regenerated before it can be approved.

A payslip is not a salary record: asking this endpoint for a salary-record id answers 404 naming the resource that serves it.

bulk_approve_invoices.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.write`

Approve multiple invoices in a single request. Provide either `filter` — the server resolves and approves every matching invoice still pending approval (use for "approve all pending", optionally narrowed by date range or contact; no need to list ids) — or an explicit list of `ids` (1–100). Each invoice is approved independently: a failure on one does not block the others. Returns 204 when all succeed, 207 (with the failed ids) when some could not be approved, 422 when none could.

filter.description: Optional scoping filter for the invoices to approve. This endpoint ALREADY targets only invoices pending approval, so for "approve all pending" pass an EMPTY object `{}` — do NOT add a payment status. Narrow only by date range (start_date/end_date) and/or contact (contact_id). The server resolves and approves every matching unapproved invoice (up to 200 per call). Provide either `filter` or `ids`, not both.

ids.description: Explicit invoice ids to approve (alternative to `filter`, for a specific selection). Max 100.

bulk_archive_contacts.description:
**Required permission:** `contacts:contacts.write`

Archives multiple contacts in a single request. Archived contacts are hidden from default listings but can be retrieved with the `archived` filter.

Contacts that do not exist or are already archived are silently skipped. If any contact ID belongs to a different account the request fails with 400.

contact_ids.description: List of contact IDs to archive (24-char hex ObjectId each)

bulk_cancel_invoices.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.write`

Cancels multiple invoices (facturas) in a single request; returns 207 when some could not be cancelled (e.g. drafts or already cancelled) and 422 when all fail. Use when the user asks to cancel several invoices at once, or "cancelar facturas en bloque". See the single-invoice cancel endpoint for individual cancellations.

ids.description: List of invoice IDs to cancel

bulk_delete_contacts.description:
**Required permission:** `contacts:contacts.write`

Permanently deletes multiple contacts in a single request. This action cannot be undone.

Contacts that do not exist are silently skipped. If any contact ID belongs to a different account the request fails with 400. Existing documents linked to deleted contacts retain the contact name for display, but the live association is removed.

contact_ids.description: List of contact IDs to delete (24-char hex ObjectId each)

bulk_delete_invoices.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.write`

Deletes up to 100 invoices in a single request. Returns 207 when some could not be deleted and 422 when all fail.

ids.description: List of invoice IDs to delete

cancel_invoice.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.write`

Cancels a sales invoice, preventing further edits or payments. Returns 200 on success and 422 when the invoice state does not allow cancellation (e.g. already paid or voided). Use when the user asks to cancel or void an invoice, or says "quiero anular esta factura" or "cancelar factura".

convert_document.summary: Convert a document to another type
convert_document.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.write`

Converts an existing document into a new document of a different type. For example, convert an estimate into an invoice or a sales order into a waybill.

The source document remains unchanged; a new document of the target type is created and linked to the source. Not all conversion pairs are supported — the available conversions depend on the document types configured in your account.

This is the only way to create a document that preserves the parent-child relationship with the source. For partial conversions (e.g. invoicing only a portion of a proforma), use this endpoint to create the linked document and then update the resulting document's line quantities or prices accordingly.

source_type.description: Type of the source document to convert from

target_type.description: Type of the target document to convert to

date.description: Issue date for the new document in ISO 8601 format

due_date.description: Due date for the new document in ISO 8601 format

number_line_id.description: Identifier of the numbering series to use

notes.description: Internal notes for the new document

draft.description: Whether to create the new document as a draft

create_accounting_account.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:chart-of-accounts.write`

Creates a new accounting account in your chart of accounts. Accounting accounts categorize financial transactions for reporting and comply with your country's accounting plan.

The response returns the new account `id`.

Provide `number` to assign a specific account number. Provide `prefix` alone to auto-assign the next available number within that group.

**AI assistant note:** `prefix` is the chart-of-accounts GROUP code (1–4 digits), NOT the full account number. To create an account with a specific number, use the `number` field and set `prefix` to the group it belongs to (the leading digits of the number, e.g. for number 70000013 use prefix 7000).

prefix.description: Chart-of-accounts group code (1–4 digits). The full account number is auto-assigned within this group when `number` is absent. Must be 1–4 digits.

number.description: Exact account number to assign (e.g. 70000013). Must start with `prefix`. When provided the number is used as-is and must be unique; otherwise the next available number in the group is assigned.

name.description: Display name for the accounting account

description.description: Optional description of the account purpose

color.description: Hex color code for UI display

create_bank_movement.summary: Create one or multiple manual bank movements
create_bank_movement.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:banks.write`

Creates one or multiple manual bank movements on a banking account.

Pass a single JSON object to create one movement, or a JSON array (up to 100 items) to create movements in bulk. All items are validated upfront; if any fails validation, nothing is created.

Movements are created with `origin: manual` and a `pending` reconciliation status, ready to be matched against documents via the `/match` endpoint.

Holded Wallet accounts are not supported by this endpoint.

amount.description: Movement amount in the banking account currency. Positive for credits (money in), negative for debits (money out). Decimal as string.

value_date.description: Value date of the movement (ISO 8601 date or date-time). Defaults to today if omitted.

balance.description: Bank balance after the movement in the banking account currency. Decimal as string.

oneOf.description: Bulk movements — array of up to 100 items. All items are validated upfront; if any fails validation, nothing is created.

amount.description: Movement amount. Positive for credits, negative for debits. Decimal as string.

create_banking_account.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:banks.write`

Creates a new banking account in your account. Banking accounts represent your bank accounts, credit cards, cash registers, or payment gateways — they track cash positions and transaction history.

The response returns the new banking account `id`. You must specify a `type` (bank, card, gateway, or cash) and optionally provide bank details like IBAN and BIC.

Accounts created through this endpoint are **manually-managed**: they have no bank connection and won't auto-sync movements. To onboard a bank-connected account, use the in-app Banking onboarding flow.

name.description: Display name for the banking account

type.description: Banking account type

creditor_id.description: SEPA creditor identifier for direct debits

create_booking.description:
**Required permission:** `crm:booking-services.write`

**Workflow**: Always call `GET /api/v2/booking-locations/{locationId}/slots` first to retrieve available time slots. Use the exact `from` value of a slot as `date_time`. Collect any fields from the `form` array before calling this endpoint.

Creates a new booking for a specific service at a location. Requires a valid location, service, date/time, timezone and language.

date_time.description: Booking start time as ISO 8601 datetime. Use the exact `from` value returned by the slots endpoint (e.g. 2024-01-15T10:30:00+01:00). The timezone offset must match the slot timezone — do not convert to UTC.

create_contact.description:
**Required permission:** `contacts:contacts.write`

Creates a new contact in your account. Contacts represent the people and companies you do business with — customers, suppliers, leads, debtors, or creditors.

At minimum you must provide a `name`. The `type` field controls how the contact appears in your accounting (e.g. client, supplier). If omitted, the contact is created without a type and can be classified later.

The response returns the new contact `id`. Use it to create invoices, purchases, or any other document linked to this contact.

name.description: Contact full name or company name

trade_name.description: Commercial or trade name, if different from legal name

is_person.description: True if the contact is an individual, false if a company

type.description: Contact classification

client_record.description: Number of the accounting account (chart of accounts) used when this contact acts as a client

supplier_record.description: Number of the accounting account (chart of accounts) used when this contact acts as a supplier

sepa_ref.description: SEPA mandate reference for direct debit collections

sepa_date.description: Date the SEPA direct debit mandate was signed

value.description: Value stored in the custom field

defaults.description: Default settings applied to documents created for this contact

payment_day.description: Default fixed payment day of the month

sales_tax.description: Default sales tax keys applied to sales documents

purchases_tax.description: Default purchases tax keys applied to purchase documents

numbering_series.description: Default numbering series applied to new documents of each type created for this contact. Each value must be a valid numbering series ID; invalid or unrecognized IDs are silently ignored (stored as null).

salesorder.description: Numbering series ID for sales orders

order.description: Numbering series ID for purchase orders

proform.description: Numbering series ID for proforma invoices

Creates a new contact group.

create_credit_note.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.write`

Creates a new credit note for a contact. Credit notes reduce the balance owed by a customer — typically issued to correct an error, apply a discount, or cancel a previously issued invoice.

You must provide a `contact_id` referring to an existing contact. Include line items in the `items` array. The response returns the new credit note `id`.

date.description: Issue date in ISO 8601 format. Accepts date (YYYY-MM-DD) or datetime (e.g. 2026-01-15T00:00:00+00:00)

due_date.description: Due date in ISO 8601 format. Accepts date (YYYY-MM-DD) or datetime (e.g. 2026-01-15T00:00:00+00:00)

notes.description: Internal notes visible only to your team

body.description: Rich-text content printed on the credit note

type.description: Kind of line. `product` and `service` are billable lines whose amount (`units` × `price`, less `discount`, plus `taxes`) is added to the document total. `title` is a section-header line that shows only its `name` and carries no amount — it does not contribute to the total. Other values are special-purpose lines. Omit this field for an ordinary priced line item.

product_id.description: Identifier of an existing catalog product to link this line to. The id is stored as a reference associating the line with the product (used for stock and reporting). Each line field (`price`, `taxes`, ...) is taken as sent; api2 stores the line values you provide and does not itself read them back from the product record. Leave unset for a free-text line that is not a catalog product.

variant_id.description: Identifier of the variant of `product_id` to link this line to. Requires `product_id`. Leave unset for a line without variant.

service_id.description: Identifier of an existing catalog service to link this line to. When provided, the line type is automatically set to `service`. Leave unset for a free-text line that is not a catalog service.

taxes.description: Tax keys applied to this line. When omitted, the contact default tax applies, or no tax if the contact has none.

supplied.description: Whether this line is a supply expense (suplido) paid on behalf of the client. Excluded from the tax base.

value.description: Value stored in the custom field

number.description:
Custom document number. Use only if you do not want to assign the number via one of the numbering series created in Holded (e.g. to replicate exactly the number from another platform). The value is saved as-is, without correlativity validation. If this field is sent, number_line_id is ignored.

Warning: do not use a value that matches the format of an existing numbering series. The series keeps its own counter regardless of manually assigned numbers -- e.g. if a series is at number 24 and you manually create a document with 27, the series will keep issuing 25, 26, and when it reaches 27 it will try to create a number that already exists: the request will fail and the series will have lost its correlativity and order. If you need custom numbering, use a prefix or format that does not match any active series, or manage every document in that series with number_line_id.

number_line_id.description: Identifier of the numbering series used to automatically assign the next correlative number. This is the recommended option, as it preserves the document order and correlativity. If both fields are sent, number takes priority and number_line_id is ignored.

payment_method_id.description: Identifier of the default payment method

design_id.description: Identifier of the design template to apply to the document

create_credit_note_payment.summary: Create a payment for a credit note
create_credit_note_payment.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.write`

Records a payment against the credit note. The payment amount is deducted from the pending balance.

You can record partial payments by specifying an amount less than the total outstanding. The credit note status is automatically updated to paid when the pending balance reaches zero.

date.description: Payment date in ISO 8601 format

treasury_id.description: Identifier of the treasury account. If omitted, the account default treasury is used.

create_employee_time.summary: Create a time entry for an employee
create_employee_time.description:
**Required permission:** `team:time-tracking.write`

Creates a completed time tracking entry with start and end times.

The response returns the new time entry `id`.

## Error handling
When this tool returns a 422 error, the error message contains the reason. Surface it verbatim to the user and stop — do NOT offer to retry with different parameters. Common errors:
- **"start_at cannot be a future date"**: future time entries are not allowed — inform the user and stop.
- **"overlaps with an existing time entry"**: there is already an entry for that period — inform the user and stop.

start_at.description: Start time in the user's local timezone. Use ISO 8601 format without UTC offset (e.g. 2026-03-01T09:00:00) so the API interprets it in the account timezone. Do not use +00:00 — it will shift the stored time by the account's UTC offset. Date-only (e.g. 2026-03-01) is also accepted.

end_at.description: End time in the user's local timezone. Use ISO 8601 format without UTC offset (e.g. 2026-03-01T17:00:00) so the API interprets it in the account timezone. Do not use +00:00 — it will shift the stored time by the account's UTC offset. Date-only (e.g. 2026-03-01) is also accepted.

pauses.description: Optional list of pauses within the time entry. Each pause must be within the start/end range.

start_at.description: Pause start time in local time without timezone offset (e.g. 2026-03-01T14:00:00). Do NOT append +00:00 or Z.

end_at.description: Pause end time in local time without timezone offset (e.g. 2026-03-01T15:00:00). Do NOT append +00:00 or Z.

create_payslip.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:payrolls.write`

Creates payslips (nóminas) in bulk for a collection of employees in a given liquidation period.

This creates PAYSLIPS, NOT salary records (registros salariales) — use /api/v2/salary-records for those. Never call this endpoint when the user asks for a salary record, and never call the salary-record endpoint when the user asks for a payslip.

Creation is asynchronous and the response body is empty: there is no job id and no endpoint to poll for status or results. An employee id that cannot be resolved for the account, whose liquidation period is locked, or who already has an approved payslip of any kind overlapping the liquidation month (the calendar month of liquidation_period_start_date), is silently skipped for that employee only — the rest of the batch still succeeds. The same happens for every employee in the batch when the account has no payroll scheme or its default accounting account cannot be resolved. If every employee id in the batch is skipped, the response is still 202 and there is no way to confirm what was actually created.

Generating over an approved payslip is not supported: the approved payslip must be deleted first, explicitly, by the user.

This endpoint is not idempotent: calling it twice with the same employees and period creates duplicate draft payslips. Do not retry a call whose outcome is unknown.

Resolve a name or code to an id first via GET /api/v2/employees — never invent an id. One request creates one payslip per employee. Duplicate ids are collapsed to a single payslip.

liquidation_period_start_date.description: Any date within the liquidation period to create payslips for (ISO 8601, YYYY-MM-DD). The whole calendar month is used — day-of-month is ignored. Periods before 2025 are not supported.

create_payslip_payment.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:payrolls.write`

Records a payment against a payslip that already exists, deducting the amount from its pending balance. Partial payments are allowed (an `amount` below the outstanding total).

All three body fields are optional: an omitted `amount` defaults to the full pending balance, and an omitted `date` defaults to the payslip's own payment date (the start of the month after the liquidation period ends, or the contract end date when it falls inside that period). `bank_account_id` ties the movement to a treasury account, and must belong to this account.

Payroll is what the Human Resources gem sells, so this endpoint requires it to be active on the account and answers 402 when it is not.

A payslip is not a salary record: asking this endpoint for a salary-record id answers 404 naming the resource that serves it.

export_inbox.summary: Convert incoming document into a purchase document
export_inbox.description:
**Required permission:** `inbox:inbox.write`

Converts an incoming document into the purchase document its scan detected, with the data the scan extracted: supplier, dates, lines, taxes, totals and accounting account.

The resulting document type is not chosen by the caller, it comes from the scan: a purchase invoice (`purchase`), a purchase refund (`purchaseRefund`), a purchase order (`purchaseOrder`) or a receipt (`receipt`). Read it on the incoming document before converting.

The document is created as a draft when the account is configured to create documents in draft mode, when the incoming document came from a bank transaction, or when the fiscal validation (TicketBAI, VeriFactu) rejects a direct creation. The `draft` field of the response says which of the two happened, so a draft can be approved afterwards.

Conversion needs a document type, an issued date and — for every type but `receipt` — a supplier already linked to the incoming document. When the scan could not resolve one of them the answer is 422: fill it in with `PUT /api/v2/inbox/{incomingDocumentId}` and convert again.

An incoming document is converted once: converting an already converted one answers 409 instead of creating a second document.

Two permissions are required: writing on the inbox, and writing on the area that owns the document the scan detected — `accounting:purchases` for `purchase`, `purchaseRefund` and `receipt`, `inventory:purchase-orders` for `purchaseOrder`. Holding only the inbox one answers 403.

Required permission scopes: `inbox:inbox.write`, `accounting:purchases.write`.

**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.read`

Returns invoices in your account whose document number matches the given value.

The match is **fuzzy autocomplete**: partial prefixes (e.g. `F260`) return all invoices that start with that token, and minor typos are tolerated. Results are scored by relevance and limited to the authenticated account. Draft, deleted and cancelled invoices are excluded.

Results are cursor-paginated: the response includes a `cursor` value and a `has_more` boolean. Pass the `cursor` to the next request to fetch the following page.

parameters.name: document_number
parameters.description: Document number to look up. Supports prefixes (e.g. `F260`) and tolerates minor typos.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of invoices to return per page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor returned by the previous response. Omit to start from the first page.

get_banking_account.summary: Get a banking account by ID
get_banking_account.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:banks.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single banking account by its unique identifier.

The response includes the current balance, bank details (IBAN, BIC), synchronization status, and archived state.

get_booking.description:
**Required permission:** `crm:booking-services.read`

Returns a single booking identified by its unique ID.

get_booking_location_slots.summary: Get available slots for a location
get_booking_location_slots.description:
**Required permission:** `crm:booking-services.read`

Returns available time slots for a specific service at a location on a given day. The response also includes the booking form fields (under `form`) that must be collected from the user before calling Create a booking.

get_contact.description:
**Required permission:** `contacts:contacts.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single contact by its unique identifier.

The response includes all contact data: billing address, shipping addresses, contact persons, custom fields, default invoicing settings, social networks, and accounting records. Use this endpoint when you need the complete contact profile — for list views, prefer the List contacts endpoint which returns the same fields but paginated.

get_contact_attachment.description:
**Required permission:** `contacts:contacts.read`

Downloads a single attachment from a contact.

The response body contains the raw file bytes. Use the `Content-Disposition` header to obtain the original file name.

get_contact_group.description:
**Required permission:** `contacts:contacts.read`

Returns a single contact group by its ID.

get_contact_portal_link.summary: Get client portal link for a contact
get_contact_portal_link.description:
**Required permission:** `contacts:contacts.read`

Generates a portal access link for a specific contact. The link allows the contact to access their client portal where they can view documents. The link expires after 2 days.

get_credit_note.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single credit note by its unique identifier.

The response includes line items, payment status and breakdown, custom fields, and the source document if the credit note was created from an invoice.

get_credit_note_attachment.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.read`

Downloads a specific attachment from a credit note. The response contains the raw binary content of the file.

get_credit_note_pdf.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.read`

Downloads the credit note as a PDF file. The response Content-Type is `application/pdf`.

The PDF is generated using the template configured in your account settings.

get_employee.description:
**Required permission:** `team:employees.read`

Returns a single employee by its ID.

get_employee_contract.description:
**Required permission:** `team:employees.read`

Returns all fields of the employee's active contract. Use this as the first step before updating a contract field: fetch the current data here, then send ALL fields back to the PUT endpoint modifying only what you want to change. Field names in this response match exactly the field names expected by the PUT endpoint.

get_employee_time.description:
**Required permission:** `team:time-tracking.read`

Returns a single employee time tracking entry by its ID.

get_estimate.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:estimates.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single estimate by its unique identifier.

The response includes line items, custom fields, pipeline stage, and the source document if the estimate was converted from another document.

get_estimate_attachment.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:estimates.read`

Downloads a specific attachment from an estimate. The response contains the raw binary content of the file.

get_estimate_pdf.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:estimates.read`

Downloads the estimate as a PDF file. The response Content-Type is `application/pdf`.

The PDF is generated using the template configured in your account settings and reflects the current state of the estimate.

get_event.description:
**Required permission:** `crm:events.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single CRM event by its unique identifier.

get_expenses_account.summary: Get an expenses account by ID
get_expenses_account.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:expenses-accounts.read`

Retrieves the details of a single expenses account by its unique identifier.

The response includes the account name, color, accounting number, and archived status.

get_funnel.description:
**Required permission:** `crm:funnels.read`

Returns a single funnel by its ID.

get_inbox.summary: Get an incoming document by ID
get_inbox.description:
**Required permission:** `inbox:inbox.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single incoming document by its unique identifier.

get_invoice.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single invoice by its unique identifier.

The response includes line items, payment status and breakdown, custom fields, pipeline stage, and the source document if the invoice was converted from an estimate or sales order.

get_invoice_attachment.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.read`

Downloads a specific attachment from an invoice. The response contains the raw binary content of the file.

get_invoice_pdf.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.read`

Downloads the invoice as a PDF file. The response Content-Type is `application/pdf`.

The PDF is generated using the template configured in your account settings. It reflects the current state of the invoice, including any updates made after creation.

get_invoice_recurring.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single recurring invoice by its unique identifier.

get_invoicing_forecast.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:cashflow.read`

Returns the full details of a single invoicing forecast by its unique identifier. An invoicing forecast represents a scheduled payment milestone on an estimate or purchase order.

Use when the user asks for the details of a specific cashflow forecast by id.

Distinct from the List endpoint: this returns one complete forecast record rather than a paginated collection.

get_lead.description:
**Required permission:** `crm:deals.read`

Returns a single lead by its ID.

get_ledger_entry.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:daily-ledger.read`

Retrieves a single ledger entry (asiento contable) by its ID, including every debit/credit line that makes up the entry.

get_payment.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:payments.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single payment record by its unique identifier.

The response includes amount, date, status, reconciliation status, and the linked contact and source document.

get_payment_method.summary: Get a payment method by ID
get_payment_method.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoicing-settings.read`

Returns a single configured payment method by its ID. The ID comes from the 'id' field in the list endpoint response. Note: this returns a configured payment method (manual or connected gateway such as Stripe, PayPal, GoCardless, Square, Monei, or Wallet) — not an individual transaction. Use /api/v2/payments/{id} to fetch a specific payment transaction.

get_payslip.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:payrolls.read`

Returns a single payslip with the breakdown the payroll engine computed for it: earning lines, deductions, employer contributions, the contribution bases and the net the employee receives.

A payslip (Spanish *nómina*) is NOT a salary record (*registro salarial*), which is served by `/api/v2/salary-records`. Ids of both look identical, so asking this endpoint for a salary-record id returns 404 naming the resource that does serve it.

Money and rates are decimal strings. Percentages are expressed as the number, so "12.50" means 12.5%.

get_payslip_pdf.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:payrolls.read`

Generates and returns the PDF Holded's payroll engine produces for a payslip.

A payslip (Spanish *nómina*) is NOT a salary record (*registro salarial*), which is served by `/api/v2/salary-records`. Ids of both look identical, so asking this endpoint for a salary-record id returns 404 naming the resource that does serve it.

get_price_list.summary: Get a price list by ID
get_price_list.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:rates.read`

Retrieves the details of a single price list (rate) by its unique identifier.

The response includes the price list name and optional description.

get_product.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:products.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single product by its unique identifier.

The response includes variants, stock levels across warehouses, custom fields, tax configuration, and pricing information.

get_product_image.summary: Get a product image by ID
get_product_image.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:products.read`

Retrieves a single image from a product by its image identifier.

The response includes the image URL, available sizes with dimensions, position, and description.

get_product_main_image.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:products.read`

Retrieves the main (first) image of a product. Returns 404 if the product has no images.

get_product_stock.summary: Get stock availability for a product
get_product_stock.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:products.read`

Returns the stock availability of a product, broken down into total, available, reserved and in-transit quantities across all warehouses, plus the physical stock stored in each warehouse.

Reserved stock represents units committed to pending sales orders. In-transit stock represents units incoming from purchase orders. Available stock equals total minus reserved.

get_product_stock_transit.summary: Get stock in transit for a product
get_product_stock_transit.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:products.read`

Returns the stock in transit for a product, including per-document movement details.

Each movement represents a document (purchase order, sales order or production order) that affects the product's transit stock. Incoming movements come from purchase orders. Compromised movements come from sales or production orders.

For pack products, the response aggregates transit data from all component products.

get_production_order.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:production-orders.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single production order by its unique identifier.

get_proforma.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:proforms.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single proforma invoice by its unique identifier.

The response includes line items, custom fields, pipeline stage, and the source document if the proforma was converted from another document.

get_proforma_attachment.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:proforms.read`

Downloads a specific attachment from a proforma. The response contains the raw binary content of the file.

get_proforma_pdf.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:proforms.read`

Downloads the proforma invoice as a PDF file. The response Content-Type is `application/pdf`.

The PDF reflects the current state of the proforma.

get_project.description:
**Required permission:** `projects:projects.read`

Returns a single project by its ID.

get_project_summary.description:
**Required permission:** `projects:projects.read`

Returns the summary of a project by its ID.

get_project_time.description:
**Required permission:** `projects:projects.read`

Returns a single project time tracking entry by its ID.

get_purchase.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:purchases.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single purchase invoice by its unique identifier.

The response includes line items, payment status and breakdown, custom fields, and the source document if the purchase was created from a purchase order.

get_purchase_attachment.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:purchases.read`

Downloads a specific attachment from a purchase. The response contains the raw binary content of the file.

get_purchase_order.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:purchase-orders.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single purchase order by its unique identifier.

The response includes line items, delivery tracking information, custom fields, and pipeline stage.

get_purchase_order_attachment.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:purchase-orders.read`

Downloads a specific attachment from a purchase order. The response contains the raw binary content of the file.

get_purchase_order_pdf.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:purchase-orders.read`

Downloads the purchase order as a PDF file. The response Content-Type is `application/pdf`.

get_purchase_order_received_items.summary: Get received items for a purchase order
get_purchase_order_received_items.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:purchase-orders.read`

Returns the items that have already been received for this purchase order.

The response includes received quantities and pending quantities for each line item, so you can track receipt progress.

get_purchase_refund.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:purchases.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single purchase refund (compra rectificativa) by its unique identifier.

The response includes line items, payment status and breakdown, custom fields, and the source purchase document if the refund was created from an existing purchase.

get_purchase_shipment.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:purchase-shipments.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single purchase shipment by its unique identifier.

The response includes line items, custom fields, and warehouse information.

get_receipt_note.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single receipt note by its unique identifier.

The response includes line items, payment status and breakdown, custom fields, and the source document if the receipt note was created from a sales receipt.

get_receipt_note_attachment.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.read`

Downloads a specific attachment from a receipt note. The response contains the raw binary content of the file.

get_receipt_note_pdf.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.read`

Downloads the receipt note as a PDF file. The response Content-Type is `application/pdf`.

The PDF is generated using the template configured in your account settings.

get_recurring_schedule.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.read`

Returns the occurrence schedule for a recurring invoice, including past converted, skipped, and future pending dates.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Upper date boundary (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to one year from today.

get_remittance.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:remittances.read`

Retrieves the full details of a remittance by its unique identifier. A remittance groups multiple invoices or purchases into a single SEPA direct debit or credit transfer for batch processing.

The response includes the list of documents bundled in the remittance, each with its contact, amount, and payment status.

get_salary_record_form_data.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:payrolls.read`

Returns the defaults needed to create a salary record: the top-level result/counterpart account (`default_accounting_account_id`, e.g. "465 Remuneraciones pendientes de pago") and the default payroll lines (`default_lines`) with the accounting account, tax key and description per line type, resolved from the account's payroll scheme.

Call this before creating a salary record and use the returned accounting account IDs — never ask the user for them. They come from here, or from the employee's `payroll_accounts` when configured (employee-specific accounts take precedence).

Amounts in `default_lines` are placeholders ("0") and must be replaced with the amounts the user provides.

get_salary_record_pdf.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:payrolls.read`

Returns the PDF uploaded for a salary record (Spanish *registro salarial*). A salary record is a manually entered accounting record, not a document produced by Holded's payroll engine, so it has no exported PDF of its own: if no file has been uploaded, the response is 422.

A salary record is NOT a payslip (*nómina*), which is served by `/api/v2/payslips`. Ids of both look identical, so asking this endpoint for a payslip id also returns 404.

get_sales_channel.summary: Get a sales channel by ID
get_sales_channel.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:sales-channels.read`

Retrieves the details of a single sales channel by its unique identifier.

The response includes the channel name, color, accounting number, and archived status.

get_sales_order.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:sales-orders.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single sales order by its unique identifier.

The response includes line items, shipping tracking information, custom fields, pipeline stage, and shipped item quantities.

get_sales_order_attachment.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:sales-orders.read`

Downloads a specific attachment from a sales order. The response contains the raw binary content of the file.

get_sales_order_pdf.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:sales-orders.read`

Downloads the sales order as a PDF file. The response Content-Type is `application/pdf`.

get_sales_order_shipped_items.summary: Get shipped items for a sales order
get_sales_order_shipped_items.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:sales-orders.read`

Returns the items that have already been shipped for this sales order.

The response includes shipped quantities and dates for each line item, so you can track fulfillment progress.

get_sales_receipt.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:receipts.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single sales receipt by its unique identifier.

The response includes line items, payment status and breakdown, custom fields, and pipeline stage.

get_sales_receipt_attachment.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:receipts.read`

Downloads a specific attachment from a sales receipt. The response contains the raw binary content of the file.

get_sales_receipt_pdf.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:receipts.read`

Downloads the sales receipt as a PDF file. The response Content-Type is `application/pdf`.

get_service.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:services.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single service by its unique identifier.

The response includes pricing, tax configuration, sales channel assignment, and duration.

get_task.description:
**Required permission:** `projects:projects.read`

Returns a single task by its ID.

get_tax_per_country_sorted_keys.summary: Get sorted tax keys by country and section
get_tax_per_country_sorted_keys.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:taxes.read`

Returns the ordered list of tax keys applicable for a given country and ecommerce section. Combines default country rules with section-specific overrides.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. ES, FR, DE)

parameters.name: section
parameters.description: Ecommerce section (all|shopify|prestashop|woocommerce|amazon|wix|stripe). Defaults to "all" when omitted.

get_time_off.summary: Get a time off request (absence / holiday)
get_time_off.description:
**Required permission:** `team:time-off.read`

Returns a single time off request (absence, holiday, vacation, sick leave, etc.) for the specified employee.

parameters.name: timeOffId
parameters.description: Time off request ID (24-character hexadecimal ObjectId)

get_usage.description:
**Required permission:** `developers:usage.read`

Returns the current month API usage for the API.

get_usage_by_type.description:
**Required permission:** `developers:usage.read`

Returns the current month API usage for the given type.

get_warehouse.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:warehouses.read`

Retrieves the details of a single warehouse by its unique identifier.

The response includes the warehouse name, contact information, address, and whether it is the default warehouse.

get_warehouse_stock.summary: Get stock levels for a warehouse
get_warehouse_stock.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:warehouses.read`

Returns the stock levels for all products stored in a specific warehouse.

The response includes each product's ID, variant ID (if applicable), and current stock quantity. Use this endpoint to audit inventory or synchronize stock with external systems.

get_waybill.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:shipments.read`

Retrieves the full details of a single waybill by its unique identifier.

The response includes line items, shipping tracking information, custom fields, and pipeline stage.

get_waybill_attachment.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:shipments.read`

Downloads a specific attachment from a waybill. The response contains the raw binary content of the file.

get_waybill_pdf.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:shipments.read`

Downloads the waybill as a PDF file. The response Content-Type is `application/pdf`.

get_webhook.description:
**Required permission:** `developers:webhooks.read`

Retrieves a webhook by its unique identifier.

get_webhook_events.description:
**Required permission:** `developers:webhooks.read`

Returns all supported webhook event types grouped by domain.

list_accounting_accounts.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:chart-of-accounts.read`

Returns the list of all accounting accounts in your chart of accounts.

The response includes each account's number, name, and group. Use this endpoint to discover available accounts before creating ledger entries.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Filter accounts with activity from this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Filter accounts with activity up to this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

parameters.name: include_empty
parameters.description: Include accounts with no transactions when true

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Case-insensitive partial search on account name or number

list_all_employee_times.description:
**Required permission:** `team:time-tracking.read`

Returns a paginated list of all employee time tracking entries for the account.

Results are cursor-paginated: the response includes a `cursor` value and a `has_more` boolean. Pass the `cursor` to the next request to fetch the following page. Default page size is 50, configurable up to 200.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor for pagination. Use the value returned in the previous response to fetch the next page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of items to return

list_all_project_times.description:
**Required permission:** `projects:projects.read`

Returns a paginated list of all project time tracking entries for the account.

Results are paginated with `limit` and `cursor` parameters. Default page size is 50, configurable up to 200.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor returned by the previous response. Omit to start from the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of items to return

list_all_time_offs.summary: List all time off requests (absences / holidays)
list_all_time_offs.description:
**Required permission:** `team:time-off.read`

Returns time off requests (absences, holidays, vacations, sick leave, etc.) across all employees in the account, ordered by start date descending. The `start_date_from` / `start_date_to` range is required.

parameters.name: time_off_type_id
parameters.description: Filter by absence / time off type (e.g. holiday, sick leave, vacation)

list_banking_account_bank_movements.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:banks.read`

Returns a cursor-paginated list of raw bank movements for a banking account, with the bank-reported amount, balance after the movement, value date and reconciliation status. Use this endpoint to build reconciliation flows, cash-flow analysis, balance alerts or banking dashboards. Unlike Payment records (available at `/api/v2/payments`), which link bank movements to invoices and documents, this endpoint exposes the raw entries that come from the bank statement. Results are ordered by value date descending (then by id descending to break ties). Returns an empty list for cash-type accounts (their movements live in the ledger, not the bank statement) — use `GET /api/v2/treasury/accounts/{id}/cash-movements` instead.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned by the previous page

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of movements per page. Defaults to 50, maximum 200.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on the movement value date (ISO 8601 date or date-time)

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on the movement value date (ISO 8601 date or date-time)

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Reconciliation statuses to filter by: 'pending' (not reconciled), 'reconciled' (fully matched), 'partial' (partially matched), 'forced_reconciled' (manually marked).

list_banking_account_cash_movements.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:banks.read`

Returns a cursor-paginated list of ledger entries for a cash-type banking account. Use this endpoint to list cash register movements — entries created manually or automatically from payments linked to a cash account. This endpoint only works for accounts of type cash; for bank, card, or gateway accounts use `/api/v2/treasury/accounts/{id}/bank-movements` instead (which returns raw bank-statement entries from providers).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned by the previous page

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of movements per page. Defaults to 50, maximum 200.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on the movement accounting date (ISO 8601 date or date-time)

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on the movement accounting date (ISO 8601 date or date-time)

list_banking_accounts.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:banks.read`

Returns a cursor-paginated list of banking accounts in your account.

Use `archived=true` to retrieve only archived accounts, `archived=false` for only active accounts, or omit the parameter to return both. Use the `cursor` returned by `ApiListResponse` to fetch the next page; `limit` defaults to the standard list page size and is capped at the API-wide maximum.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of banking accounts to return per page

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter banking accounts by account type. Allowed values: `bank` (bank account), `card` (credit or debit card), `gateway` (payment gateway such as Stripe or PayPal), `cash` (cash register / petty cash).

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Filter by archived state. `true` returns only archived accounts, `false` returns only active accounts. Omit to return both (default).

list_booking_locations.description:
**Required permission:** `crm:booking-services.read`

Returns all booking locations for your account. Locations are not paginated — all are returned in a single response.

list_bookings.description:
**Required permission:** `crm:booking-services.read`

Returns a paginated list of bookings for your account.

Results are cursor-paginated: the response includes a `cursor` value and a `has_more` boolean. Default page size is 50, configurable up to 200 with `limit`.

You can filter by date range and service.

To query bookings for a single day pass the same date for both `start_date` and `end_date` (e.g. `start_date=2024-01-15&end_date=2024-01-15`). A date-only value for `end_date` automatically includes the full day up to 23:59:59.

When `items` is an empty array and `has_more` is false, there are no bookings matching the given criteria — this is a definitive result, do not retry with different parameters.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Filter bookings starting from this date. Accepts ISO 8601 datetime (e.g. 2024-01-01T00:00:00+00:00) or date only (e.g. 2024-01-01)

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Filter bookings up to this date (inclusive). Accepts ISO 8601 datetime (e.g. 2024-12-31T23:59:59+00:00) or date only (e.g. 2024-12-31). A date-only value includes the full day up to 23:59:59.

list_business_plan_goals.summary: List business plan goals vs actuals
list_business_plan_goals.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:cashflow.read`

Returns Business Plan goals for the authenticated account, one row per accounting account, broken down by month. Each month carries both the `goal` (the target the account set for itself) and the `actual` (what really happened, from the ledger) for the same period, so goal and reality can be compared without a second call.

Use when the user wants to compare a client's Business Plan targets against what actually happened, e.g. to prepare a monthly review.

Only `tree=profit_and_loss` is supported today; Cashflow goals are not available through this endpoint yet.

`start_date` must not be after `end_date`, and the range between them must not exceed 36 months.

Returns an empty list, not an error, when the account has no Business Plan configured or no goals exist in the requested range.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: Start of the reporting range (inclusive, snapped to the first day of its month)

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: End of the reporting range (inclusive — any day within the last desired month)

parameters.name: tree
parameters.description: Goal tree to query. Only "profit_and_loss" is supported today.

parameters.name: scenario_id
parameters.description: Business Plan scenario to query — see GET /api/v2/business-plan/scenarios. Defaults to the account's main scenario.

parameters.name: accounting_account_id
parameters.description: Restrict the response to a single accounting account. Omit to return every account in the tree.

parameters.name: only_with_goals
parameters.description: When true, excludes accounting accounts with no goal set anywhere in the requested range. Without it, a chart of accounts with few goals mostly returns rows with goal: null — this filters those out before pagination, so pages are not spent on empty accounts.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of accounting accounts to return per page. Defaults to 50, maximum 200.

list_business_plan_scenarios.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:cashflow.read`

**Required permission:** `team:employees.read`

If more than one employee matches, present the complete list of matches (name plus email or employee code) and let the user choose; never pick one on your own.

ALWAYS use this parameter to resolve an employee the user named — pass the user's exact text. Do NOT filter by name yourself client-side (jmespath/contains): that only sees the current page and cannot fold accents, so it misses matches and picks the wrong person. This search scans ALL employees and returns every match; if more than one comes back, present them and let the user choose.

**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.read`

The list includes payment summary fields (`payments_total`, `payments_pending`) so you can display outstanding balances without fetching each invoice individually.

Payment status: an invoice with no payment recorded is `pending`, one collected in part is `partial`, and both still owe a balance. `status=outstanding` returns the two together; `status=overdue` narrows that set to invoices whose due date has passed.

Date parameters (`start_date`, `end_date`) filter by ISSUE date; `due_date_start`/`due_date_end` filter by DUE date; all are optional and unfiltered means the whole account. Use `status=overdue` to list all unpaid invoices (pending or partial) whose due date has passed. All date parameters accept RFC 3339 (e.g. `2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00`) or date-only (`2026-01-01`).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter invoices by payment status. "pending" matches invoices with no payment recorded and "partial" those collected in part; both still owe a balance. "outstanding" returns the two together, "overdue" narrows that set to a due date already past, and "completed" returns the settled ones.

parameters.name: sort

Only the numeric code is accepted; a non-numeric value returns 400. Returns 404 if no accounting account with that number exists in the tenant. When called through the AI assistant, an account name is resolved to its code automatically before the request reaches this endpoint.

list_payslips.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:payrolls.read`

Returns payslips ordered by creation (newest first).

Results are cursor-paginated: the response carries a `cursor` value and a `has_more` boolean. Pass the `cursor` to the next request to fetch the following page.

A payslip (Spanish *nómina*) is the calculated payroll document produced by Holded's payroll engine for a liquidation period, with its own social-security and IRPF breakdown. It is NOT the same document as a salary record (*registro salarial*), which is the manually entered accounting record served by `/api/v2/salary-records`. This endpoint never returns salary records, and `/api/v2/salary-records` never returns payslips: pick the endpoint that matches the document the user actually named.

Payslips only exist in accounts that create payroll through the Human Resources gem; an account without that gem cannot create new ones, but this endpoint keeps returning the payslips it already has. An empty list therefore means either no payslips in range or an account that never used payroll.

The `start_date` / `end_date` filter applies to the accrual date, not the creation date and not the liquidation period.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor returned by the previous response. Omit to start from the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of payslips to return per page. Defaults to 50, maximum 200.

parameters.name: employee_id
parameters.description: Filter by employee. Accepts the employee name, resolved server-side to its identifier.

parameters.name: is_draft
parameters.description: Filter by draft state: `true` returns only unapproved payslips, `false` only approved ones. Omit to return both.

Accepts ISO 8601 datetime or date only (YYYY-MM-DD). A date without a time (YYYY-MM-DD) includes that whole day; a value with a time is applied exactly as sent.

parameters.name: approval_status

Returns a PNG thumbnail of the file, resized to one of a closed set of platform widths. Omitting both width and height returns the original image unresized.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Name of the file to retrieve

parameters.description: Target width in pixels. Must be one of the allowed platform presets; any other value returns 404. Omit together with height to get the original image unresized.

receive_purchase_order.summary: Receive units of a purchase order
receive_purchase_order.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:purchase-orders.write`

Registers the receipt of units for a purchase order. Internally creates a linked purchase shipment (albarán de compra) and updates the purchase order's pending units accordingly.

Provide the lines you want to receive in the `items` array. Each item references an existing purchase order line by `line_id` together with the `units` being received. Partial reception is supported: any line of the purchase order that is **not** listed in `items` remains untouched and pending, and you can call this endpoint again later to receive the remaining units.

items.description: Lines being received. Each item must reference an existing purchase order line.

line_id.description: Identifier of the purchase order line being received

units.description: Number of units being received. Must be greater than zero and not exceed the line's pending units.

date.description: Reception date in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today.

warehouse_id.description: Warehouse where the units are received. Defaults to the purchase order warehouse.

reconcile_transaction_with_document.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:banks.write`

Reconciles a bank movement.

With a `documents` payload, links the movement to one or more existing Holded documents (invoices, sales receipts, purchases, credit notes, payments, remittances, and more). Pass a single document to close it in one step, or pass multiple documents to split the movement across several entries. Every document must already exist in Holded and belong to the same account.

With an empty or missing body, marks the movement as reconciled without linking it to any document — useful to clear a movement from the pending-reconciliation list when no matching document exists in Holded.

This operation is not idempotent: reconciling the same (movement, document) pair twice returns a 422 because the document is already paid or the remaining amount is zero.

documents.description: Documents to reconcile against the bank movement. Provide one or more entries when splitting a single movement across multiple documents. Omit to mark the movement as reconciled without linking any document.

document_id.description: Identifier of the Holded document to match against

reject_estimate.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:estimates.write`

Marks the estimate as rejected. This changes the estimate status to rejected and records who rejected it.

Rejected estimates remain in your account for reference but are excluded from active pipeline views.

name.description: Name of the person rejecting the estimate

search_contacts.description:
**Required permission:** `contacts:contacts.read`

Search for contacts by name. Matches against the `name` field using prefix matching (autocomplete-style): `?name=Joh` matches `John Due`, `John Smith`, etc. Token-aware, case- and diacritic-insensitive.

The response includes a `cursor` value and a `has_more` boolean. Pass the `cursor` to the next request to fetch the following page.

The default page size is 25 contacts. You can increase it up to 100 using the `limit` parameter.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Search term matched against the contact `name` field (prefix matching, case- and diacritic-insensitive)

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor for pagination. Use the value returned in the previous response to fetch the next page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of contacts to return per page. Defaults to 25, maximum 100.

Marks the entire sales order as shipped. This creates stock movements in the associated warehouse, reducing inventory for all line items.

Use this when all items in the order are shipped at once. For partial shipments, use the ship-by-lines endpoint instead.

ship_sales_order_by_lines.summary: Ship specific lines in a sales order
ship_sales_order_by_lines.description:
**Required permission:** `inventory:sales-orders.write`

Partially ships specific line items of a sales order. Use this when you can only fulfill part of the order.

Specify which lines and quantities to ship. Stock movements are created only for the shipped items. The order remains open until all lines are fully shipped.

item_line_position.description: Zero-based position of the line item

skip_recurring_occurrence.description:

Marks a specific occurrence date of a recurring invoice as skipped so it will not be converted to an invoice.

unpause.description:

Resumes a paused time tracking session for the employee.

update_banking_account.description:
**Required permission:** `accounting:banks.write`

Updates an existing banking account (manual or bank-connected).

You can change the name, currency, accounting account, default flag, auto-sync flag and bank details (IBAN, BIC, creditor/issuer IDs).

For bank-connected accounts (synced via Bridge / Account Bridge), changing `iban`, `bic` or `currency` may disrupt incoming-movement matching — modify only when you understand the impact. The `auto_sync` flag has no effect on manual accounts.

Changing the currency does not convert existing transaction amounts — it only affects how new transactions are displayed.

name.description: Display name for the banking account

auto_sync.description: Whether to automatically sync transactions from the bank

creditor_id.description: SEPA creditor identifier for direct debits

default_account.description: Whether this is the default banking account

update_booking.description:
**Required permission:** `crm:booking-services.write`

Updates the date/time and/or custom fields of an existing booking. At least one of `date_time` or `custom_fields` must be provided.

date_time.description: New booking start time in the user's local timezone. Use ISO 8601 format without UTC offset (e.g. 2024-01-15T10:30:00) so the API interprets it in the account timezone. Do not use +00:00 — it will shift the stored time by the account's UTC offset. Date-only (e.g. 2024-01-15) is also accepted.

update_contact.description:
**Required permission:** `contacts:contacts.write`

Replaces all mutable fields of an existing contact. This is a full replacement — any field you omit from the request body will be reset to its default value.

To avoid accidentally clearing data, first fetch the contact with GET, modify the fields you need, and send back the full object. Partial updates are not supported on this endpoint.

name.description: Contact full name or company name

trade_name.description: Commercial or trade name, if different from legal name

is_person.description: True if the contact is an individual, false if a company

type.description: Contact classification

client_record.description: Number of the accounting account (chart of accounts) used when this contact acts as a client

supplier_record.description: Number of the accounting account (chart of accounts) used when this contact acts as a supplier

sepa_ref.description: SEPA mandate reference for direct debit collections

sepa_date.description: Date the SEPA direct debit mandate was signed

contact_persons.description: Linked contact persons (by their contact ID)

value.description: Value stored in the custom field

defaults.description: Default settings applied to documents created for this contact

payment_day.description: Default fixed payment day of the month

sales_tax.description: Default sales tax keys applied to sales documents

purchases_tax.description: Default purchases tax keys applied to purchase documents

numbering_series.description: Default numbering series applied to new documents of each type created for this contact. Each value must be a valid numbering series ID; invalid or unrecognized IDs are silently ignored (stored as null). Omit this field entirely to keep the numbering series already configured for this contact.

salesorder.description: Numbering series ID for sales orders

order.description: Numbering series ID for purchase orders

proform.description: Numbering series ID for proforma invoices

update_contact_group.description:
**Required permission:** `contacts:contacts.write`

Updates an existing contact group.

update_credit_note.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:invoices.write`

Replaces all mutable fields of an existing credit note. This is a full replacement — any field you omit will be reset to its default value.

To avoid accidentally clearing data, first fetch the credit note with GET, modify the fields you need, and send back the full object.

date.description: Issue date in ISO 8601 format. Accepts date (YYYY-MM-DD) or datetime (e.g. 2026-01-15T00:00:00+00:00)

due_date.description: Payment due date in ISO 8601 format. Accepts date (YYYY-MM-DD) or datetime (e.g. 2026-01-15T00:00:00+00:00)

type.description: Kind of line. `product` and `service` are billable lines whose amount (`units` × `price`, less `discount`, plus `taxes`) is added to the document total. `title` is a section-header line that shows only its `name` and carries no amount — it does not contribute to the total. Other values are special-purpose lines. Omit this field for an ordinary priced line item.

product_id.description: Identifier of an existing catalog product to link this line to. The id is stored as a reference associating the line with the product (used for stock and reporting). Each line field (`price`, `taxes`, ...) is taken as sent; api2 stores the line values you provide and does not itself read them back from the product record. Leave unset for a free-text line that is not a catalog product.

variant_id.description: Identifier of the variant of `product_id` to link this line to. Requires `product_id`. Leave unset for a line without variant.

taxes.description: Tax keys applied to this line. When omitted, the contact default tax applies, or no tax if the contact has none.

supplied.description: Whether this line is a supply expense (suplido) paid on behalf of the client. Excluded from the tax base.

design_id.description: Identifier of the design template to apply to the document

update_employee.description:
**Required permission:** `team:employees.write`

Updates basic personal data of an employee (name, email, phone, nationality, workplace, etc.). Does NOT update job title, position (puesto/cargo), or any other contract data — use the "Update contract data" endpoint for those fields.

update_employee_contract.description:
**Required permission:** `team:employees.write`

Updates the active contract of an employee. This is a full-replacement operation — ALL fields must be provided. Workflow: (1) Call GET /api/v2/employees/{employeeId}/contract to get current contract data. (2) Send ALL fields from that response back here, modifying only the ones you want to change. Use when the user asks to update "puesto", "cargo", "salario", "jornada", or any contract field. Does not modify salary history — use the salary-increase endpoints for that.

contractType.description: Regulatory contract type code (tipo de contrato SEPE)

startDate.description: Contract start date in ISO 8601 format

seniorityDate.description: Employee real seniority (antigüedad) date in ISO 8601 format; must be on or before startDate. Defaults to startDate when omitted or null

endDate.description: Contract end date; null for open-ended contracts

isManuallyActivated.description: Whether the contract was manually activated

salaryPayments.description: Number of salary payments per year

update_employee_time.description:
**Required permission:** `team:time-tracking.write`

Updates the start and end times of an existing time tracking entry.

start_at.description: Start time in the user's local timezone. Use ISO 8601 format without UTC offset (e.g. 2026-03-01T09:00:00) so the API interprets it in the account timezone. Do not use +00:00 — it will shift the stored time by the account's UTC offset. Date-only (e.g. 2026-03-01) is also accepted.

end_at.description: End time in the user's local timezone. Use ISO 8601 format without UTC offset (e.g. 2026-03-01T17:00:00) so the API interprets it in the account timezone. Do not use +00:00 — it will shift the stored time by the account's UTC offset. Date-only (e.g. 2026-03-01) is also accepted.

pauses.description: Optional list of pauses within the time entry. Each pause must be within the start/end range.

start_at.description: Pause start time in local time without timezone offset (e.g. 2026-03-01T14:00:00). Do NOT append +00:00 or Z.

end_at.description: Pause end time in local time without timezone offset (e.g. 2026-03-01T15:00:00). Do NOT append +00:00 or Z.

update_estimate.description:
**Required permission:** `sales:estimates.write`

Replaces all mutable fields of an existing estimate. This is a full replacement — any field you omit will be reset to its default value.
